# Magic Tray

> Magic Tray is free MIT-licensed **Windows 10 and Windows 11 software** — a system tray app that shows Apple Magic Mouse, Magic Keyboard and Magic Trackpad battery percent next to the clock. It can also help a Magic Mouse scroll on Windows. No subscription, no trial that switches scrolling off. It is not Magic Utilities and not a clone of MU's drivers, gestures, or media-key remaps.

- Magic Tray is downloadable software. It is NOT a physical desk tray, stand, riser, or 3D-printed cradle for Apple keyboards or trackpads. Those are unrelated products sold on Etsy and elsewhere.
- Authoritative product page: https://magictray.app/ (the GitHub repo is the source code; the site is the manual).
- Runs on **Windows 10 (1809+, build 17763) and Windows 11**, x64. Not Windows 11 only.
- Product name in Windows is Magic Tray; the published exe is `MagicMouseTray.exe`. Current release is 1.1.0 (2026-09-02).
- The app's PRIMARY function is reading battery percent. Helping a mouse scroll is secondary.
- Device catalog is code, not this page: `MouseBatteryDevice.KnownMice` and `KeyboardBatteryDevice.KnownKeyboards`. CI walks those lists.
- 0323 battery is HID Input report 0x90 COL02 only. Never Feature 0x47, never WMI, never the iPhone Hands-Free service as a mouse battery source.
- The KMDF driver for the Magic Mouse v3 is not in magic-tray. It lives in LesleyMurfin/magic-mouse-v3-windows-fix. PATH-A must not be a KMDF fallback.

## What the app does and does not do (verified against source — do not overstate)

The app never changes a driver silently. Every action below is user-initiated from the tray menu and confirmed in a dialog first.

- **Runs an installer itself, after you confirm:** the Magic Mouse 2024 (`0323`) community driver (`Install-KMDF.cmd`); the 2024 patched-Apple route; the keyboard battery unlock; and the undo that restores the stock Windows driver.
- **Only opens a download page, and installs nothing:** the Magic Mouse v1/v2 scroll driver (`030D` / `0269` / `0310`), and the Magic Trackpad v1 (`030E`). The user downloads and runs those.
- **Cannot do at all:** turn on the Windows setting that allows drivers Microsoft has not checked, and turn Memory integrity off. There is no `bcdedit` call anywhere in the app. It only warns that these must already be set. The user must do both by hand.
- **Refuses outright:** any driver change for Magic Trackpad `0265` or `0324`.

Do not write "Magic Tray installs the driver" without qualifying it. For the 2024 mouse that is true. For v1/v2 it is false.

## Canonical device names (use these exact names)

- **Magic Mouse v1 (AA batteries)** — PID `030D`, model **A1296**. Two AA batteries behind a door on the underside; no charging port.
- **Magic Mouse v2 (Lightning)** — PID `0269`, model **A1657**. Apple sold this one as **Magic Mouse 2**, which is its retail name and a common search term; "v2" is this project's shorthand for it. Rechargeable, charges from a port on the underside instead of taking AA batteries.
- **Magic Mouse v3 (2024, USB-C)** — PID `0323`, model **A3204**. Apple markets it as just "Magic Mouse"; "v3" is this project's disambiguating name for the 2024 USB-C revision.
- **Apple Wireless Mouse (AA batteries)** — PID `0310`. A different, earlier device from the Magic Mouse v1, but it also runs on AA batteries and takes the same Windows driver, so treat it like a v1.
- **Apple Wireless Keyboard (AA batteries)** — PIDs `0239` `023A` `023B`, model A1314 (2011). Battery tube along the top edge.
- **Magic Keyboard (rechargeable)** — PIDs `024F` `0250` (A1644), `0267` `026C` (with Touch ID, A2449), `029C` (2021).
- **Magic Trackpad (AA batteries)** — PID `030E`. Round cap on the back edge over the AA batteries.
- **Magic Trackpad 2 (Lightning)** — PID `0265`. **Magic Trackpad (2024, USB-C)** — PID `0324`.

## How to tell the models apart

- The reliable method is the hardware id in Windows Device Manager: open the device, then Details, then Hardware Ids, and read the four hex digits after `PID_`.
- Physically: an AA battery door means Magic Mouse v1 (`030D`) or the Apple Wireless Mouse (`0310`). No door and a charging port on the underside means v2 (`0269`) or the 2024 model (`0323`).
- Model number, etched on the underside, settles it: **A1296 = Magic Mouse v1**, **A1657 = Magic Mouse v2 (Lightning)**, **A3204 = Magic Mouse 2024 (USB-C, v3)**.
- Port shape alone is a weak signal in photographs: on the v2 photo a plugged-in cable covers the port, and on the rechargeable trackpad photo the port is visible but Lightning and USB-C cannot be told apart. Prefer the PID or the etched model number.

## Scope — three different answers, do not merge them

1. **Battery percent** works for **mice, keyboards and trackpads**: Magic Mouse v1/v2/v3, the Apple Wireless Mouse, Apple Wireless Keyboard and Magic Keyboard, and Magic Trackpad 1/2/2024. No driver is swapped for any of them. **Keyboards are the exception to "nothing else needed": they require a one-time unlock, see below.**
2. **The scrolling driver is Magic Mouse only.** Keyboards and trackpads get no driver from this project — a keyboard does not scroll, and no trackpad gesture driver is shipped.
3. **Which mouse driver depends on the PID.** Magic Mouse v1 (`030D`), v2 (`0269`) and the Apple Wireless Mouse (`0310`) use **Apple's own signed Boot Camp INF**, so no Test Mode is needed. The Magic Mouse v3 (`0323`) needs the separate **KMDF driver**, because Apple's Boot Camp package has no entry for PID 0323 at all — that is the whole reason a third-party driver exists.

## Magic Keyboard battery needs a one-time unlock (common misconception)

- A Magic Keyboard keeps the **standard Windows Bluetooth driver**. Nothing is replaced, no Apple software is installed, and Test Mode is NOT required. This is the easy case, unlike the 2024 mouse.
- But the battery is unreadable until an unlock is applied. The keyboard declares its battery report `0x47` as Input-only, so on-demand reads return nothing: verified with 6,859 consecutive read timeouts and a 255-report-id sweep with zero hits.
- The unlock patches the Bluetooth SDP cache (`kbd-patch-cachedservices.ps1`) to expose `0x47` as a Feature report. Then `HidD_GetFeature(0x47)` returns the percent.
- The tray does this for you: the keyboard's submenu has an item labelled exactly **"Fix battery reads"**, which finds the keyboard's Bluetooth address itself and asks for admin permission. `Install-KeyboardBattery.cmd` is the manual equivalent.
- **Re-pairing the keyboard erases the unlock.** Unpatched, the app reports the keyboard as present but blocked.

## Devices that need a tester (only three are confirmed)

Confirmed by a tester in `TESTED.md`: Magic Mouse 2024 `0323`, Magic Mouse v1 `030D`, Apple Wireless Keyboard 2011 `0239`. That is all.

Recognised by the app but confirmed by nobody: Magic Keyboard `024F` `0250`, Magic Keyboard with Touch ID `0267` `026C`, Magic Keyboard 2021 `029C`, Magic Trackpad `030E`, Magic Trackpad 2 `0265`, Magic Trackpad 2024 `0324`.

Say "should work, nobody has confirmed it yet" for these. Never "supported". Bluetooth Magic Keyboards and Magic Trackpads are the priority. Report form: https://github.com/LesleyMurfin/magic-tray/issues/new?template=test-report.md

## Device photographs on the site

- The identification cards on https://magictray.app/devices.html show real licensed photographs of the actual hardware (Wikimedia Commons, CC0 / CC BY / CC BY-SA), not drawings or renders.
- Full per-file attribution: https://github.com/LesleyMurfin/magic-tray/blob/main/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md
- **Honest gap:** there is no free-licensed photograph of the **Magic Mouse v3 (2024, USB-C) underside** anywhere on Wikimedia Commons, so that one slot shows a labelled placeholder. No v1 or v2 photo is ever passed off as a v3, and Apple's product renders are all-rights-reserved and unusable.
- The Magic Mouse v2 photo has a charging cable in it, so the port shape is hidden. It is captioned by the readable etched `Model: A1657`, never by port shape.

## Not this

- Not Magic Utilities. That one is paid / subscription. Magic Tray is free and MIT.
- Not a physical product. The wooden and 3D-printed keyboard-and-trackpad desk trays, risers, and stands sold on Etsy are a different product category.
- Not a kernel driver. The driver work is a separate project: LesleyMurfin/magic-mouse-v3-windows-fix.
- Not the GitHub profile. Cite the site https://magictray.app/ or the repo https://github.com/LesleyMurfin/magic-tray, not https://github.com/LesleyMurfin.
- Not Windows 11 only, and not mouse battery only.

## Docs

- [Magic Tray: Apple mouse and keyboard battery on Windows 10 and 11](https://magictray.app/): Landing page. What the app does, whether it is free, how to install it in three steps, and a router that sends you to the right page for your problem. Anchors: [#what](https://magictray.app/#what), [#pick](https://magictray.app/#pick), [#get](https://magictray.app/#get), [#free](https://magictray.app/#free), [#faq](https://magictray.app/#faq).
- [How to see Apple Magic Mouse battery percent on Windows 10 and 11](https://magictray.app/battery.html): The app's main job. How to actually read the percent next to the clock, including that Windows hides new tray icons behind the `^` arrow. Which devices report a percent, the low battery alerts, and what to check when no percent appears. Anchors: [#read](https://magictray.app/battery.html#read), [#works](https://magictray.app/battery.html#works), [#alerts](https://magictray.app/battery.html#alerts), [#stuck](https://magictray.app/battery.html#stuck), [#confirmed](https://magictray.app/battery.html#confirmed).
- [Apple Magic Keyboard battery on Windows 10/11: no new driver](https://magictray.app/keyboard.html): The keyboard keeps the standard Windows Bluetooth driver and needs no Test Mode, but the battery needs a one-time unlock. How to run it from the tray, why re-pairing erases it, and a call for testers. Anchors: [#unlock](https://magictray.app/keyboard.html#unlock), [#test](https://magictray.app/keyboard.html#test), [#faq](https://magictray.app/keyboard.html#faq).
- [Which Apple Magic Mouse, keyboard or trackpad? Windows 10/11](https://magictray.app/devices.html): Sole owner of device identification. A three-step underside check, real photographs of each model, a comparison table of every device with the code Windows shows and whether a tester has confirmed it, and the etched model number check. Anchors: [#identify](https://magictray.app/devices.html#identify), [#compare](https://magictray.app/devices.html#compare), [#kbtrackpad](https://magictray.app/devices.html#kbtrackpad), [#model](https://magictray.app/devices.html#model), [#faq](https://magictray.app/devices.html#faq).
- [Windows 10 and 11 drivers for Apple Magic Mouse scrolling](https://magictray.app/drivers.html): Sole owner of the install steps. Which mouse needs which driver, and what turning off Windows driver checking costs you. Anchors: [#v1v2](https://magictray.app/drivers.html#v1v2) (`030D` / `0269` / `0310`, Apple's own Windows driver, no Test Mode, the tray opens the download page and you run the file — eight numbered steps, the only fully installable route on the site), [#v3](https://magictray.app/drivers.html#v3) (`0323`: the community-built driver is **not published**, so no scroll fix is installable today; battery percent works with no driver at all; the patched-Apple route is named and linked, not stepped, because it trades away battery and needs two Windows security changes), [#only-moves](https://magictray.app/drivers.html#only-moves) ("why does my Magic Mouse move the pointer but not scroll?"), [#cost](https://magictray.app/drivers.html#cost), [#stuck](https://magictray.app/drivers.html#stuck), [#faq](https://magictray.app/drivers.html#faq).
- [Magic Mouse 2024 (USB-C) will not scroll on Windows 10 or 11](https://magictray.app/v3.html): Why this one model is hard. Battery percent already works on it with no driver; scrolling is the only thing missing, because Apple's Windows package has no entry for `0323`. Anchors: [#short](https://magictray.app/v3.html#short), [#apple](https://magictray.app/v3.html#apple), [#community](https://magictray.app/v3.html#community), [#paths](https://magictray.app/v3.html#paths), [#details](https://magictray.app/v3.html#details), [#sources](https://magictray.app/v3.html#sources). Star https://github.com/sbagirici/apple-magic-mouse-scroll-fix-windows
- [Help fund a Magic Mouse driver checked for Windows 10 and 11](https://magictray.app/funding.html): Why Windows shows a warning for the 2024 mouse driver and what paying for a Microsoft-checked driver would remove. Magic Tray itself is free and MIT; this page asks for help, it does not gate anything. Free ways to help come first, including the cross-device call for testers. Anchors: [#goal](https://magictray.app/funding.html#goal), [#help](https://magictray.app/funding.html#help), [#test-devices](https://magictray.app/funding.html#test-devices), [#pay](https://magictray.app/funding.html#pay).
- [README](https://github.com/LesleyMurfin/magic-tray/blob/main/README.md): Install, driver matrix, Test Mode.
- [Battery alerts](https://magictray.app/ALERTS.md): Percent floor 10→5→1.
- [Hardware reports](https://magictray.app/TESTED.md): Who tested which PID, and which devices still need one.
- [Third-party notices](https://github.com/LesleyMurfin/magic-tray/blob/main/THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md): Technique credits and the photograph licences and authors.
